items.excerpt: Brown University researchers built a physics-informed neural network that predicts how controlled-release materials dispense drugs, potentially slashing development time for therapeutic patches, bandages and implants by up to 94%.

Technion's BetaDescribe is an AI system that translates raw protein sequences into natural-language descriptions, generating evidence-based hypotheses about the functions of otherwise-uncharacterized proteins for drug discovery and biotech.

An international team at GSI/FAIR trained a deep neural network (RHINE) to model r-process heating in neutron-star mergers, letting simulations of how the universe forges its heaviest elements run far faster and more accurately.

From structural biology to particle physics, AI systems increasingly deliver results of remarkable power and accuracy — yet even their creators struggle to explain how they reach them, raising the question of what counts as understanding in science.

Judith S. Beck weighs AI mental-health chatbots against human therapists: chatbots are low-cost and available 24/7 but carry real risks, while clinicians tailor treatment with empathy and clinical judgment an LLM cannot yet replicate.

A new critique (Peter J. Denning, Taylor & Francis) argues Turing's 1950 assumption — that human intelligence can be encoded into a computer — may be wrong, contending common sense, intuition, culture and practical know-how resist formalization by AI.

Anthropic's 'Jacobian lens' reveals a hidden 'J-space' inside Claude Opus 4.6 — words that shape a model's upcoming output without appearing in it — offering the clearest glimpse yet into how LLMs represent and weigh concepts internally.
